key_insight: A minimal three-sphere model separates geometry- and friction-controlled particle trapping from fracture governed by impact conditions and particle size ratio.
engineering_relevance: The model can inform ball-milling designs by identifying collision conditions that trap and fracture brittle particles rather than eject them intact.
method: Simulate three-sphere collisions using the discrete element method (DEM).
Predict trapping with a closed-form geometric condition incorporating friction.
Evaluate fracture using Christensen-type stress-based and Weibull-type contact-force-based normalized criteria.
evidence_signal: DEM results show that critical fracture conditions vary with impact angle, obliquity, velocity, and particle size ratio, with larger size ratios requiring lower critical velocities in head-on collisions.
watch_item: The minimal three-sphere model does not establish predictive accuracy for the many-body collision environment of a full ball mill.
paper_title: Trapping and Fracture of Particles in Three-Sphere Ball-Milling Collisions
